prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Create an UNLOCKED, slightly OPEN version of this exact evil dungeon treasure chest for the same mobile game. Image 1 is the approved CLOSED LOCKED CHEST, the edit target and authoritative style/camera reference.
Keep the same footprint, squat base, dark plum timber, chunky slate-charcoal fittings, upper-left painted shading and orthographic 2:1 game perspective. Keep base/front/right edges and bottom contacts at the same locations in the composition. Preserve the stylized broad shapes and dark contours.
Change the storage state: raise the hinged lid backwards only about 25 degrees so it is clearly AJAR, not fully upright. Show a compact visible pile of a few large worn gold coins inside the dark cavity: about six readable overlapping coin shapes, some on edge, no tiny hundreds of coins. Gold should be muted ochre with simple light faces, not sparkling or bright magical treasure.
This is the FREE UNPROTECTED chest. Remove the glowing violet lock/seal and the large blocking front clasp; replace that centre front area with a simple short dark iron reinforcing plate. The chest must look usable and unlocked. Keep its sinister dungeon craftsmanship, not a heroic polished-gold pirate chest. Violet lid seam is absent because the chest is unsealed. No coins outside the box. No new padlock, eye, face, teeth, skull or creature. No extravagant extra ornaments. Do not repaint or simplify the base more than needed to remove the lock.
Mobile readability: overall chest will be displayed about 96 pixels wide. Lid opening, dark cavity and 4-6 broad coin silhouettes must remain distinct at that small scale. No microdetail. Entire object, including raised lid, inside generous clear margins.
Transparent native-alpha background. Everything outside the solid object's outline is EMPTY TRANSPARENCY. No cast shadow, floor, aura, external glow, mist, backdrop, text or checkerboard. Keep full silhouette and identical camera; no perspective convergence.
